items.label: Cisco Q4 FY2026 (08-12-2026)
items.signal_prefix: SCALE-ACROSS is the emerging motion: Cisco estimates network traffic

set.signal: SCALE-ACROSS is the emerging motion: CEO Chuck Robbins: 'we think the network traffic related to AI-based scale-across versus traditional data center interconnect is roughly 14x what it might have been before.' Three new hyperscaler design wins in Q4 — (1) a Silicon One P200-powered system for SCALE-ACROSS, the third P200 scale-across win since launch, EACH WITH A SEPARATE HYPERSCALER, with orders already received from all three in Q4; (2) a G200-powered system for scale-out; and (3) a MANAGED OPTICAL FIBER NETWORK win using Cisco's line-system technology that enables its digital coherent optics inside THIRD-PARTY equipment — strategically positioning Cisco as an alternative to an incumbent competitor. Cisco has line of sight to multiple further AI design wins over the next six months across G300, G200 and P200 silicon plus optics, and MULTI-RAIL OPTICAL SYSTEMS are 'coming soon' / beginning to deploy. Acacia took over $1B of orders in Q4 and has now shipped over 850,000 400G and over 75,000 800G coherent pluggables to date.

items.reason: The Q3 shipment comparison is not stated on this call (it came from the old file's editor note); the 14x estimate is the CEO's hedged 'we think', not a company fact.
items.evidence: we think the network traffic related to AI-based scale-across versus traditional data center interconnect is roughly 14x what it might have been before

items.label: Cisco Q4 FY2026 (08-12-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Demand breadth behind the 'networking super cycle'

set.signal: Demand breadth behind the 'networking super cycle': total Q4 product orders +35% YoY (+25% EXCLUDING hyperscale), with hyperscale orders up triple digits. Service provider and cloud orders +95%, public sector +30%, enterprise +21% (double-digit growth in every product category and geography); telco orders accelerated to over +30%. By geography, Americas +44%, EMEA +25%, APJC +19%. Networking product orders +40%, an EIGHTH consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, on triple-digit growth in service-provider routing and Acacia optics. Overall data center networking orders grew more than 35% YoY (CEO, on enterprise private data center networking: 'Q3 was in excess of 40%, I believe, and in Q4, it was in excess of 35%'); campus networking orders +20% with Wi-Fi 7 now more than 50% of wireless orders; industrial IoT has grown double digits for nine straight quarters. Enterprise Nexus switch orders tagged for AI deployments rose more than 85% SEQUENTIALLY. More than half of Cisco customers now buy both campus and data center networking.

items.reason: The CEO said 'more than 35%'; the Q3 comparison was his hedged recollection ('I believe') about enterprise private data center networking.
items.evidence: Q3 was in excess of 40%, I believe, and in Q4, it was in excess of 35%

items.label: Cisco Q4 FY2026 (08-12-2026)
items.signal_prefix: FY2027 guidance: revenue $72.2-73.4B and non-GAAP EPS

set.signal: FY2027 guidance: revenue $72.2-73.4B and non-GAAP EPS $5.05-5.11 — CFO Mark Patterson: 'accelerating to 15% on the top line, 17% on the bottom line'. Backing out the $7.5B of hyperscale AI revenue, the CFO said, 'you get to the core business growing at about 10%, which is obviously significantly faster than that investor day' model. Q1 FY2027 guidance: revenue $18.0-18.2B, non-GAAP gross margin 65-66%, non-GAAP operating margin 35.5-36.5%, EPS $1.32-1.34, tax ~18.5%. Management expects a SLIGHT GROSS MARGIN HEADWIND through FY2027 because the super cycle is shipping high hardware volumes and shifting revenue mix toward hardware, but frames operating margin (~35% for FY2027, a company high-water mark) as the better profitability indicator — hyperscaler business carries minimal incremental operating expense, so even lower-gross-margin business is highly profitable. Security and observability go from low single-digit FY2026 growth to high single digits in FY2027; services turn positive to low single-digit growth.

items.reason: '4-6% long-term model' and 'at the midpoint' were the analyst's (Amit Daryanani) words; the CFO only compared the ~10% core growth with the investor-day model.
items.evidence: you get to the core business growing at about 10%, which is obviously significantly faster than that investor day that we have done awfully long ago at this point

items.label: Cisco Q4 FY2026 (08-12-2026)
items.signal_prefix: MEMORY COST PASS-THROUGH AND SUPPLY POSTURE: price

set.signal: MEMORY COST PASS-THROUGH AND SUPPLY POSTURE: price increases contributed about FIVE POINTS of top-line revenue growth in Q4, with roughly four to five points planned for FY2027 (weighted to the first half as prior increases lap). Increases are SINGLE DIGIT, applied to HARDWARE ONLY (not software) and targeted at products with higher memory content. Cisco's exposure is structurally lower than server vendors': memory is roughly 15-20% of its bill of materials versus about two-thirds for server-heavy vendors, since ~95% of what Cisco sells is not a server. Internally, more than 30 programs target memory-utilization efficiency — Wi-Fi 7 memory utilization was cut 50% within about 90 days. Management describes price increases as 'a last resort', with customers accepting them as an industry rather than a Cisco issue. On supply: no significant lead-time issues, strategic agreements and advance purchase commitments in place, strategic inventory being built, investments 'like we did in Nanya on the memory side', and direct dealing with TSMC (no middleman) across wafer, substrates, assembly and test.

items.reason: The CFO said 'investments'; 'equity' is not stated on the call.
items.evidence: You have seen us make investments like we did in Nanya on the memory side.

items.label: Cisco Q4 FY2026 (08-12-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Demand drivers management expects to sustain the super cycle

set.signal: Demand drivers management expects to sustain the super cycle, per Chuck Robbins: hyperscaler AI build-out; telcos investing ahead of AI scale-across bandwidth; enterprise network modernization for AI; an 'impending MYTHOS effect' customers are preparing for (term used on the call but not defined, cited alongside AI readiness and quantum readiness); and downstream QUANTUM preparation. Customers are running last-day-of-support (LDOS) analysis on gear that cannot be patched, and Cisco says the Mythos-related pipeline has increased meaningfully — showing up as a network refresh but 'probably underneath viewed as a cybersecurity spend' — while the CEO also said 'we haven't seen a massive amount of impact from Mythos yet' and 'we have not seen material Mythos or last day of support in our numbers to date, but the pipeline is building'. Enterprise budgets are being REPRIORITIZED within existing envelopes rather than expanded, with AI/Mythos/quantum readiness treated as non-optional in the way cybersecurity spend has been for the last three to five years. Cisco's newest systems (Secure Routers, smart switches, wireless controllers, secure firewall platforms) are POST-QUANTUM-CRYPTOGRAPHY compliant. Q4 also closed the Galileo Technologies and Astrix Security acquisitions.

items.reason: The CEO's hedge that Mythos / LDOS demand is not yet in the numbers was lost.
items.evidence: we have not seen material Mythos or last day of support in our numbers to date, but the pipeline is building

items.label: Cisco Q4 FY2026 (08-12-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Record close to FY2026. Q4 revenue $17.3B (+18% YoY)

set.signal: Record close to FY2026. Q4 revenue $17.3B (+18% YoY) with PRODUCT revenue $13.5B (+24%) and services $3.8B (flat); non-GAAP net income $4.9B and non-GAAP EPS $1.22, both records and each +23%. Non-GAAP gross margin 66.3% (-210bps YoY, +30bps QoQ) with PRODUCT gross margin 64.8% (-270bps) driven by higher hardware mix and MEMORY COSTS, partially offset by productivity and price increases; services gross margin 71.6% (+80bps). Non-GAAP operating margin 35.9%; operating cash flow $5.4B (+27%). FY2026: record revenue $63.3B (+12%), non-GAAP operating margin 34.8% (+40bps), non-GAAP net income $17.2B (+13%), non-GAAP EPS $4.33 (+14%) — the highest revenue, operating margin and earnings per employee in 30 years. Networking revenue growth accelerated to 28%, security +14%, collaboration +12%.

items.reason: Verifier: capital returns, the dividend increase and the remaining buyback authorization are financing terms (skill section 2); the operating results stay.
items.evidence: We increased our dividend for the 15th consecutive year in FY 2026
